limits: Standalone operators using sealed donor Keccak and scalar-comparator sources; original nine DSOs are neither modified nor loaded.

All three backends share a logical-lane-zero parser (the even physical lane for split32); this isolates state mapping and does not measure production eta four-thread consumer, ballot compaction, retry scheduling or complete APIs.
Split32 uses the sealed production permutation <1,false>, IOTA_WORD_LOAD=0, with a harness byte stream; this does not establish every production module compiler policy.

Split32 retains padded pairs and drains a whole warp; work artifacts distinguish logical blocks, absorb permutations, executed squeeze permutations and drain dummy permutations, plus padded-state work.

Dummy split32 rounds still write the shared byte buffer. Counts describe source-level primitive calls per state, not hardware instructions. Padding states are zero initialized and receive harness padding; wholly inactive warps exit uniformly.
A fixed 832/1088-byte transcript SHAKE256 case measures final-hash arithmetic, not complete verification.
Kernel event times include output initialization, decoding, logical trace and physical work writes; no end-to-end production-module speedup is established.
ON/OFF changes this audit harness only. OFF uses eight squeeze blocks, rather than a production-module early-stop configuration.
Work.logical_squeeze is the count of raw permutation calls for op0. For SHAKE/sampling, absorb counts only full input blocks; the padded first output permutation is counted as squeeze.
Forced-rejection cases are synthetic refill/exhaustion fixtures, not normal FIPS vectors.
256 deterministic input rows are tiled across each batch; empty-input SHAKE has one unique row. Three processes reuse the same corpus.
All requests/bytes and counters are checked before and after each timed variant; individual intermediate timed outputs are not separately checked.
Shared stage lock and pre/post idle GPU samples are used; continuous exclusive GPU use is not claimed.
CPU-only self-tests do not establish CUDA compilation or device correctness; those must pass on the server before acceptance.
